references.text: Describes which animals may be brought as offerings to the Lord, establishing the basis for what is considered a valid sacrificial animal.
Concerns the requirements for animals offered to the Lord, including that they must be without blemish to be accepted.
Continues directly from verse 9 and explains that an animal vowed to the Lord cannot be exchanged.
Elaborates on the principle that what is devoted to the Lord is most holy and belongs to the Lord.
Confirms that the firstborn of cattle, sheep, and goats are holy to the Lord and cannot be redeemed.
Establishes the principle that the firstborn is consecrated to the Lord.
Concerns vows made to the Lord and the importance of keeping them, including voluntary offerings.
